issues.title: Lahaina water use permit applications and TIG report
issues.summary: On August 20, the Maui County Board of Water Supply voted unanimously to approve the Temporary Investigative Group (TIG) report on water use permit applications in the Lahaina surface and groundwater management area, to be sent to the state Commission on Water Resource Management (CWRM). The report found requests of almost 9 million gallons a day, 213% of reported existing use, and called the sustainable yield numbers indefensible as regulatory rules. It recommends reviewing surface and groundwater applications together and a full monitoring program before non-conditional permits.

issues.title: Lahaina banyan tree recovery
issues.summary: As of September 9, eight of 16 planned supports have been added to the banyan tree's side branches, about two weeks earlier. An arborist will return with a spider lift for more trimming once it is scheduled. The chair said the tree will stay closed another year and a half, after a July decision that no one will enter its park for two years so it can heal.

issues.title: Proposed Maui County passenger ferry to Molokaʻi and Lānaʻi
issues.summary: At a September 17 community meeting, county staff said the Maui Ferry project is "not a done deal" and that a draft environmental assessment will be released for public comment. The passenger-only service would be run by a private operator, with Molokaʻi service hoped for by early 2029; the Council will set fares. issues.title: Mokuʻula restoration master plan
issues.summary: At the August 6 meeting, a commissioner said they were very supportive of the restoration project, and the commission took no action. The department's first step is removing the courts and parking lot, with archaeological and cultural monitors on all work and topsoil placed over cleared areas. It is working with the Salvation Army to acquire land the group still owns, and the master plan, being developed until June 2027, will build in the commission's 2019 recommendations.

issues.title: Ending apartment vacation rentals and hotel rezoning of 48 properties
issues.summary: On October 23, the Council voted down Resolutions 26-160 and 26-161, which would have sent more condo properties to the Maui Planning Commission for hotel zoning review. The chair said vacation rentals are being phased out of apartment districts, and new hotel districts exist for properties where continued rental use is appropriate. On September 29, the Council sent a list of coastal apartment-zoned properties to the Commission under Resolution 26-129, five to four.

issues.title: Yearly USGS water monitoring agreement
issues.summary: On October 23, 2026, the council passed Bill 134 by 8–0, letting the mayor sign a joint funding agreement with the U.S. Geological Survey to continue the water resources program. The agreement runs October 1, 2026 through September 30, 2027 and costs $225,920, with $199,720 from the water department, already in the fiscal year 2027 budget. The program collects rainfall, streamflow and groundwater data on Maui and Molokaʻi, and the agreement is renewed yearly.
